I’ll update the broadcast lifecycle so a live scheduled broadcast can be returned to draft, and ensure every launch creates a new active schedule. I’ll inspect the relevant backend and Broadcasts UI conventions, then make the focused change without running tests.
The change includes both a Broadcasts UI control and backend state handling, so I’m applying the repository’s frontend component and test-design guidance before editing.
The existing API already permits the `active → draft` transition. I’ll expose it only for broadcasts that have not yet created a send run, and on launch delete all stored schedules before activating and creating the new one. This preserves sent/running broadcasts while fixing the paused-schedule relaunch path.
I’ve made the lifecycle changes. I’m adding one focused Kea-logic test for the new “return to draft” action; it guards the user-visible state transition without introducing a browser test.
The implementation is complete: the summary now offers “Edit broadcast” only before any send run exists, and relaunch deletes stale schedules before creating the new schedule. I also added a focused logic test for the draft transition and verified the tracked diff has no whitespace errors.
Implemented the broadcast recovery flow.

- Scheduled broadcasts with no send run can now be returned to draft via an “Edit broadcast” button.
- Relaunching removes all existing schedules before activating and creating the new schedule, so a paused schedule cannot silently block delivery.
- Added a focused Kea logic test for returning a broadcast to draft.

I did not install dependencies or run the test suite, per request.
